name: te5_billow
purpose: P4a the void's dense ink smoke and P4b the moon's grey-silver smoke (one puff per particle life)
notes: Flipbook 4x4 OneShot: frame k shows the puff at life fraction (k + 0.5) / 16. A volumetric puff ray-marched in 3D (Beer-Lambert, key light upper front left with a shadow march, multiple-scattering lift, rim light from behind, sky from above): born dense and compact (visible radius ~0.19 of the cell), billows out in rolling cauliflower lobes (radius ~0.38 by frame 11), softens, and from frame ~11 thins into curling veils (texture mean alpha falls ~70 % over frames 11-15 by itself). Opaque core (alpha 1) in frames 0-10. Baked light comes from the upper left: keep the particle's Rotation within about +-20 deg (not 0-360) or the light turns with it. The puff grows inside its cell, so the emitter's Size curve should grow less than for te5_smoke (see the recommended settings).

name: te5_wisp
purpose: P11 silver wisps rising off the wearer's shoulders and back
notes: Flipbook 4x4 OneShot (life ~1.6-2.2 s = 7-10 fps): thin twisted ribbons of smoke advected through curl noise -- a slender rising thread at birth that curls into incense-like tendrils (bright where a fold is edge-on, a veil where it is face-on) and thins out. OneShot, not Loop: the wisp's own life (thread -> curls -> fade) matches the particle's, every particle starts thin at the body, and a loop would have to fold back on itself (a visible cycle at 8-10 fps). It rises toward the TOP of the cell: keep Rotation within about +-15 deg.

name: te5_mistbank
purpose: P7 the low mist bank round the dais rim
notes: One image (FlipbookLayout None): a soft low fog bank ~0.8 of the image wide and ~0.3 tall, densest along its middle line (where the floor cuts a particle born on it), billowy and thinning upward, lit from above, in soft horizontal layers. A single image because the mist lives 6-8 s: a flipbook at 2-3 fps would step visibly. Keep Rotation within about +-5 deg so the bank stays level.
